clue.text: First catch your uncooked lobster !

parts.note: echoes the old cookery-book instruction 'first catch your hare', applied to a raw shellfish of the spiny-lobster kind that must be caught before it is cooked

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction: before anything else, go and catch the raw lobster.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the saying 'first catch your hare', traditionally credited to Mrs Beeton's Victorian cookery book, here applied to a lobster-like shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawfish is the spiny lobster or crayfish, a clawed crustacean eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Islet formed entirely of stone?

parts.note: a rock is a stone
all means wholly, entirely

explanation.surface: A small island made of nothing but stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Rockall is a tiny uninhabited rock in the North Atlantic, west of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny isolated rock in the North Atlantic, disputed between the UK and Ireland.

clue.text: Toss her a towel at the pool

indicators.note: to toss is to throw about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Throwing someone a towel at the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss' rearranges HER A TOWEL; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool of water where animals come to drink is a waterhole.

clue.text: Stick in this notice over the entrance?

definitions.meaning: to be inherent, to reside within something
a sign above a doorway directing people to come in this way

explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to exist within as a permanent quality; split, it is a sign pointing inside.

clue.text: He wants no more birthdays if he's to succeed

definitions.text: He wants no more birthdays if he's to succeed

parts.words: He wants no more birthdays if he's to succeed
parts.note: the person next in line can be displaced by a nearer heir, so he hopes no more children are born

explanation.surface: An ageing man who would rather not celebrate any more birthdays if he is to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birthdays' suggests his own ageing; it means births of others who would take precedence in the succession.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir whose right to inherit can be overtaken by the birth of a closer relative.

clue.text: It's single for a duel

parts.note: a duel is fought one against one, described by the set phrase 'single ___', so the clue asks for the word completing that phrase

explanation.surface: A remark that a duel is a one-on-one affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Single combat is the fixed phrase for a fight between two individuals, as in a duel.

clue.text: Have done with a scrap before getting a pasting

definitions.meaning: an order to stop doing something

definitions.text: a scrap before getting a pasting
definitions.meaning: what one does to a piece of paper with scissors before gluing it in a scrapbook

explanation.definitionFit: To stop something, and literally to snip out a clipping before gluing it down.

clue.text: VIP on the range

definitions.meaning: a very important person, a bigwig
on a shooting range, a large-calibre discharge of a gun

explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is called by this, and literally it is a large-calibre discharge at a shooting range.

clue.text: Valued retainers — rest are with us anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in any haphazard order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Loyal servants say the others are on our side regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges REST ARE and US; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A much-valued servant or helper is often called a treasure.

clue.text: Wound the spirit

definitions.meaning: to wound without killing, as in Macbeth's 'We have ... the snake, not kill'd it'
the national spirit of Scotland, whisky

explanation.definitionFit: To scotch is an old verb for injuring or cutting, and Scotch is whisky, a distilled spirit.

clue.text: Plot for the Carry On series ?

definitions.text: Plot for the Carry On series ?

parts.words: Plot for the Carry On series
parts.note: the storyline of the British comedy films is full of scheming, and 'carry on' also means to conduct a secret love affair

explanation.surface: Someone asking what storyline the Carry On comedy films should follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a long-running series of saucy British comedies; 'carry on' as a verb means to have an illicit affair, which is another sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret scheme is a plot, and a clandestine love affair is also called by this word.

clue.text: Head lock-keeper

parts.note: read as a keeper of the locks on one's head, that is a clip holding strands of hair in place

explanation.surface: The senior keeper at a canal lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock-keeper' suggests a canal official; here locks are tresses of hair, and the head is where they grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair clip that keeps strands of hair in place on the head.

clue.text: Producer's parts once taken by the rector

definitions.text: Producer's parts once taken by the rector

parts.words: Producer's parts once taken by the rector
parts.note: a tenth share of a farmer's produce was formerly paid to the parish clergyman as a church levy

explanation.surface: A film producer's roles being given to a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Producer' suggests film or theatre; here it is a farmer, whose crops were once taxed a tenth for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a tenth of farm produce, paid as a levy to support the parish church and its clergy.

clue.text: Shakespeare's simple constable could have been bent .

definitions.meaning: the bumbling constable in Measure for Measure bears this name
the joint in the middle of the arm is what bends it

explanation.definitionFit: Elbow is the foolish constable in Measure for Measure, and the arm joint is where the arm bends.

clue.text: One's firm friend goes after record. See the description

indicators.note: goes after places the following pieces behind the record

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
one's read as 'I is', I being one
co is short for company, a firm
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A loyal colleague follows a record, with a pointer to a description elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese, and the answer is the adjective describing matters of bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a bishop, whose diocese is called a see.

clue.text: Got a ruler out for the Controller

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fetched a ruler to show the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals that GOT A RULER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or official that controls a process is a regulator.

clue.text: Such Dutch talk is relatively severe

definitions.text: Such Dutch talk is relatively severe

parts.words: Such Dutch talk is relatively severe
parts.note: a stern lecture is said to come from a 'Dutch uncle', and an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: Remarks from the Netherlands come across as rather harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'talk like a Dutch uncle' is to scold frankly; 'relatively' hints at the family relation of uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for an uncle's manner, as in the stern talk of a Dutch uncle.

clue.text: He's not the promoter's right-hand man

definitions.text: He's not the promoter's right-hand man

parts.words: He's not the promoter's right-hand man
parts.note: a boxing promoter's fighter who leads with the left rather than the right

explanation.surface: Someone who is not the chief assistant of a business promoter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-hand man' suggests a deputy; the promoter is a boxing promoter, and the fighter is left-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer, who leads with the right fist and punches with the left.

clue.text: No dice, odd last drink causing unseemly behaviour .

indicators.note: last puts the drink at the end of the answer after the shuffled letters
odd means peculiar or out of normal order, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Refusing to play, and then a strange final drink, leading to bad conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges NO DICE into INDECO, and 'last' places RUM after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety, conduct that breaks good manners.

clue.text: Easily drawn, say, Donald's plastic bathroom decoration ?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as the answer

parts.note: a plastic tile for the bathroom showing Donald, the cartoon duck: a duck tile

explanation.surface: A plastic bathroom ornament of Donald, the sort easily sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donald' is Disney's Donald Duck, giving DUCK, and a bathroom decoration is a TILE; said together they sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ductile metal can be stretched out into wire, that is, drawn without breaking.

clue.text: His heroes were all for one, and vice versa

definitions.text: His heroes were all for one, and vice versa

parts.words: His heroes were all for one, and vice versa
parts.note: the motto 'all for one and one for all' belongs to the Three Musketeers, created by a French novelist

explanation.surface: A tribute to an author whose characters were utterly loyal to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas wrote The Three Musketeers, whose heroes swore 'all for one, one for all'.

clue.text: Odd way a driver reached his destination

indicators.note: arranged in an odd way, so the letters of the phrase are mixed up

explanation.surface: A motorist took a strange route but got there.
explanation.definitionFit: To have got to the place one was heading for.

clue.text: Much-loved Eliot hero Daniel lost direction on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read bottom to top, backwards
lost means dropped, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: Daniel Deronda is the title hero of George Eliot's last novel
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A beloved hero of George Eliot loses his bearings as he climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes N from DERONDA, leaving DERODA; 'on the way up' turns it to read ADORED.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply, cherished.

clue.text: Seal a hiding-place, the first of 8

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store or hiding-place

indicators.note: the first of picks the opening letter of the answer to the clue numbered 8

explanation.surface: Sealing up a secret store, the first of several.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' points at the answer to 8 down, TREASURES; 'the first of' takes its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachet is a seal stamped on a letter or document, hence a mark of distinction.

clue.text: Footwork to keep one in trim

definitions.text: Footwork to keep one in trim

parts.words: Footwork to keep one in trim
parts.note: not dancing or boxing steps but cosmetic work on the feet, keeping the toenails trimmed

explanation.surface: Exercise for the feet that keeps a person fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footwork' and 'in trim' suggest fitness; the work is done on the feet, and the trimming is of toenails.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic treatment of the feet and toenails, including cutting the nails.

clue.text: Caesar's ghostly rendezvous

parts.note: in Julius Caesar, the dead Caesar's ghost tells Brutus 'thou shalt see me at' a battlefield in Macedonia

explanation.surface: The place where Caesar's spirit arranged to meet someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian battlefield where Caesar's ghost promises to meet Brutus in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Experience again what is about to-be

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through something a second time, in memory or in fact.

clue.text: Go to ground like Brer Fox

definitions.meaning: to hide and keep out of sight
in the Uncle Remus tales, Brer Fox 'he lay low' after setting the Tar-Baby trap

explanation.definitionFit: To hide and keep quiet; Brer Fox famously 'lay low' in the Uncle Remus stories.

clue.text: The Spanish gold found in part of wall in Manoa

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a dado is the lower part of an interior wall
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Spanish gold discovered in a section of wall in a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is placed inside DADO to give DORADO, after EL. Manoa was the legendary golden city sought by explorers in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled city of gold was identified by explorers with the legendary city Manoa on Lake Parime.
